title: 30 Days of Back-and-Forth
subtitle: A play-first screen-time plan for families: 30 short lessons, 30 easy plays and plain words for tricky moments
format: Written program, sold and delivered automatically. (1) Online program ($27): 30 daily lesson emails (each lesson under 300 words, plus one play and one plain-word script), a welcome email, automatic check-ins on days 3, 10 and 30, and a day-31 wrap-up (emails/). (2) Instant-download workbook, included: 89 pages in Color and Low-ink, each in US Letter and A4, with 141 type-in fields that work in free Adobe Acrobat Reader, plus START HERE.pdf as file 1 (downloads/). (3) Amazon KDP paperback of the whole program: 92-page black-and-white interior, 8 x 10 in (paperback/). (4) Free lead magnet '7 Days of Play First' (3-page PDF, Letter + A4) and its 7-email funnel (funnel/). No video, no coaching, no calls.

short_description: A written 30-day plan by email: one short lesson, one easy play and plain words for a tricky moment each day, plus a printable workbook. Ages 1–12.
long_description:
A written 30-day program for ages 1 to 12, by email with a printable workbook: 30 short lessons, 30 easy plays and 38 plain-word scripts for tricky moments.

Each morning, one short email comes. It has a lesson you can read in about three minutes and one easy play. It also gives you plain words for one tricky moment, like a show that won’t end, ‘I’m bored’ or a long car ride.

Nothing is banned. Screens get a steady spot in the day, with the same time and the same ending. They are never a prize or a punishment. The rest of the day fills up with play and back-and-forth talk.

Your 89-page workbook comes in Color and Low-ink, in US Letter and A4. You can type in it with free Adobe Acrobat Reader. Inside are plans, trackers, weekly check-ins, a bank of scripts, a family plan and a Day 30 certificate.

Every play has a starting age, an easier and a harder version and a 2-minute version for tired days. 22 of the 30 plays need no prep, and the rest take about 2 minutes. Every play uses things you already have and follows our published safety rules.

It costs $27, about 90¢ a day. It is parent education, not medical advice. There are no videos, calls or coaching. 14-day money-back guarantee: a full refund if you email us within 14 days of purchase and have completed no more than 30% of the lessons.

compliance_notes: Name: renamed from the retired ‘The 30-Day Screen Reset’ (brand/ORIGINALITY.md A4, retired-names list); ‘reset’ is kept out of every title, keyword, URL and email. No health or medical claims: the program is described as parent education; it never says it treats, changes, prevents or undoes anything, and disclaimers avoid clinical words. No condition or diagnosis terms in any lesson, email, listing or keyword. No pre-launch social proof: lines like ‘many parents say’ or ‘most families find’ were removed because no family has used the program yet. No trademarked program names: talk moves are in plain words (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add one, offer a choice, follow their lead, sing and gesture). Citations limited to the BRAND.md list, stated as associations: WHO 2019 (Days 2, 12), AAP 2016 (Day 3), Brushe et al. 2024 (Day 2, ‘a link, not proof’), Delgado et al. 2018 (Day 21); listed on a Sources page. No real brands, apps, devices, schools or products; the tablet is a generic, sleepy, never-evil character; the Tablet Slept dog is not named (Biscuit is retired, ORIGINALITY B4). Screens are never earned or taken away (CUSTOMER-VOICE #13); no fear words. Every play: starting age in months, prep/mess/play-time/materials icons, easier/harder pair, 2-minute tired version, talk line and a safety note under rule 4 (grown-up present, toilet-paper-tube test for under-3s, no balloons, no cords or scarves long enough to wrap a neck, water supervised, no choking-hazard foods or small round vegetables, flashlights with screwed-shut battery covers, never cover a charging device, grown-ups handle knives/stove/chargers). 100% of plays need nothing to buy. Pediatrician line on the stage/age pages, Day 2, Day 13 and Day 29. Faceless: no video, no founder photo, no calls; emails never promise personal replies. No merchandise and no slogans in this product; the paperback end page uses only the kept brand tagline C1 on a parent-facing page (never on children’s items). Copyright line: ‘© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.’ Version footer ‘Version 1.0 · September 2026’ on every page and email. Every marketing email carries the CAN-SPAM footer placeholder [BUSINESS MAILING ADDRESS], unsubscribe and pause links, a reward-free “share the free printable” link to playbeforepixels.com/30-days/start (no referral program exists, so no email promises a reward; business/GROWTH-ENGINE.md §4) and a next-product recommendation. Check the paperback interior and cover against KDP’s current templates and cover calculator before upload; Chromium PDFs are RGB with embedded fonts. The logo is the final kit in brand/logo/ (if the v2 logo lands, re-run make.sh; nothing is hard-coded). Customer panel (September 28, 2026, panel.md): food plays (Days 2, 5, 26) now say to check for food allergies first; the play-basket page no longer lists a scarf; Sleeping lion tickles only if the child enjoys them; the Day 6 warning has a see-it option (sand timer, two fingers) and big-kid game rounds; the Day 13 reconnect offers space before a hug.
